title: Sizing & Protecting HikariCP Connection Pools
prompt: Your inventory Spring Boot service (10 pods, each with `HikariCP maximumPoolSize=20`, `connectionTimeout=30000`) runs on an 8-core PostgreSQL primary. Normally `GET /items/{id}` takes 4 ms at 1,500 RPS. When an admin triggers an unindexed `GET /items/search?q=widget` query taking 12 seconds at just 25 RPS, the entire service locks up with `HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms`—even for healthy `/items/{id}` lookups. Diagnose the starvation and harden the pool.

spark.summary: A single unindexed query taking 12 seconds consumes all 20 HikariCP connections in under a second, causing every fast 5 ms query to block for `connectionTimeout` (30s) and cascading into Tomcat thread exhaustion.
spark.keyTakeaway: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, enforce strict DB `statement_timeout` and JDBC `socketTimeout`, size pools using Little's Law (`(cores * 2) + spindles`) rather than inflating them, and isolate slow endpoints with bulkheads.

decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.

explanation.foundation: Protect the 8-core PostgreSQL primary and keep `/items/{id}` `p99 < 25 ms` with four controls:
